## Peer-to-peer attachments arrive in meshmsg

This release adds explicit, content-verified file and folder transfer without changing meshmsg's peer-to-peer model. Small signed offers travel through Iroh Gossip, while attachment bytes are transferred directly with Iroh Blobs.

### Highlights

- **Share files:** `meshmsg share ./report.pdf`
- **Share folders:** directories are packaged as deterministic tar snapshots
- **Manual downloads:** receiving an offer never downloads content automatically
- **Verified transfers:** BLAKE3 content hashes verify data while it streams
- **Persistent availability:** shared content and pins survive daemon restarts
- **Interoperability:** download either a meshmsg signed offer or a raw Iroh BlobTicket
- **Compatible messaging:** existing signed text messages continue to decode normally

### Safety and limits

- Downloads require an explicit output path and never overwrite an existing file or directory.
- File and archive blobs are limited to 1 GiB.
- Directory sharing rejects symlinks, special files, unsafe names, and excessive path depth or entry counts.
- Archive extraction rejects traversal paths, links, duplicate entries, case collisions, and file/directory collisions.
- Attachment work is concurrency-limited and staged data is cleaned up safely after failure or cancellation.

### Documentation

The README is now a concise introduction and quick start. Detailed guides live under `docs/`:

- installation and source builds;
- command and JSON usage;
- attachment behavior and security;
- daemon operations and systemd;
- benchmarking;
- development and release checks.

### Install

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eldar-Ahmadov/meshmsg/main/install.sh | bash
```

Or install this exact source revision after the release tag is available:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/Eldar-Ahmadov/meshmsg.git \
  --tag v0.1.7 --locked --force
```

### Current limitations

Attachments are plaintext to anyone who obtains the signed offer. Persistent attachment pins do not yet have automatic expiry or an `unshare` command.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Eldar-Ahmadov/meshmsg/compare/v0.1.6...v0.1.7
